# Checked payment aggregates (issue #2013)

Oracle: `XRPLF/xrpld-private`, tag `3.4.1`, commit
`d147fccf54a500fce586522f28d6044c37fd8d29`. The release-delta base is
`4a4fded2eba11427c48ce3f24d9c1aea5e7a9d17` (3.4.0).

`checked_add_oracle.json` was generated by compiling `checked_add_oracle.cpp`
against the clean local oracle's actual `MathUtilities.h`. The same signed
inputs drive Go's XRP and MPT additions, sorted book sums, and sorted flow
sums. Null means an unrepresentable sum, including intermediate overflow in
ascending order. Exact signed extrema remain valid.

To regenerate from the repository root, set `oracle` to that local checkout:

```sh
oracle=/path/to/rippled-worktrees/v3.4.1-oracle
test "$(git -C "$oracle" rev-parse HEAD)" = d147fccf54a500fce586522f28d6044c37fd8d29
test -z "$(git -C "$oracle" status --porcelain)"
c++ -std=c++17 -I "$oracle/include" internal/tx/payment/testdata/checked_add_oracle.cpp -o /tmp/checked-add-oracle
/tmp/checked-add-oracle > internal/tx/payment/testdata/checked_add_oracle.json
```

The header's compile-time assertions also check subtraction. `checkedSub` has
no changed payment consumer in this release, so this fix does not introduce a
Go subtraction API. Go addition tests cover the applicable signed boundary
contract. IOU arithmetic continues to use the existing Number context and
rounding; a separate regression checks smallest-first summation under all
three mantissa scales.

## Consumer map

Paths and lines below refer to the pinned C++ checkout.

| C++ consumer | Go equivalent | Overflow outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Steps.h:511-545`, XRP/MPT checked addition | `EitherAmount.checkedAddWithNumberContext`, `AddWithNumberContext` | Optional failure or typed dry-strand error |
| `BookStep.cpp:1056-1066`, shared sorted sum | `amountMultiset.sum` | Typed `flowError(tecPATH_DRY)` |
| `BookStep.cpp:1105`, reverse full input/output | `BookStep.Rev` full-take staged sums | Discard strand |
| `BookStep.cpp:1134`, reverse partial input | `BookStep.Rev` partial-take input sum | Discard strand |
| `BookStep.cpp:1242`, forward full input/output | `BookStep.Fwd` full-take sums | Discard strand |
| `BookStep.cpp:1258`, forward partial output | `BookStep.Fwd` partial-take output sum | Discard strand |
| `BookStep.cpp:1275`, forward cache reconciliation | Both `BookStep.Fwd` reconciliation sums after removing the last output | Discard strand |
| `StrandFlow.h:761`, output across selected strands | `Flow` checked output sum each iteration | Return `tecPATH_DRY`, no sandbox |
| `StrandFlow.h:767`, send total with SendMax | `Flow` checked input sum when SendMax exists | Return `tecPATH_DRY`, no sandbox |
| `StrandFlow.h:806-809`, final output/input totals | Already-checked final output and SendMax input; final input sum when SendMax is absent | Return `tecPATH_DRY`, no sandbox |

`Steps.h` and `StrandFlow.h` are under `include/xrpl/tx/paths/detail/`;
`BookStep.cpp` is under `src/libxrpl/tx/paths/`.

The book helper is shared by XRP/IOU, IOU/XRP, IOU/IOU, XRP/MPT,
MPT/XRP, IOU/MPT, MPT/IOU, and MPT/MPT books, including AMM liquidity.
The flow tests vary input/output assets independently, including XRP/XRP,
with and without SendMax and partial payments.

Book overflow bypasses the MPTokensV2 `std::overflow_error` offer-removal
handler (`BookStep.cpp:846`). `StrandFlow.h:297` catches the typed flow error,
discards the strand's sandbox, and retains permanent offer removals already
discovered. Another strand may succeed. If all strands are dry, partial
payments return `tecPATH_DRY` and full payments return `tecPATH_PARTIAL`.
Flow aggregate failures return before merging the current iteration's
removals, preserving only removals from completed iterations. With no
SendMax, input is checked at finalization after those iterations. No new
amendment gates any of these checks.

## Reachability and evidence limits

XRP supply is at most `10^17` drops, below `MaxInt64`; fabricated XRP step
totals near `MaxInt64` test a safeguard, not a demonstrated valid-ledger
exploit. MPT supply per issuance is bounded by `MaxInt64`, but a reverse
book pass can price multiple individually valid offers before limiting the
source's input. The MPT regression uses two offers requesting `5e18` input
each and a 50% input transfer fee: each step input is `7.5e18`, while the
input issuance's total supply remains `MaxInt64`. The second reverse sum
overflows before the send limit can trigger a forward retry. The failed
strand preserves the offers, holdings, issuance totals, and reserve counts.

The direct forward-book test intentionally supplies more MPT holdings than
the issuance total; it exercises the output safeguard, not reachable
production funding. Synthetic flow steps similarly bypass funding/request
limits to isolate the aggregate checks and sandbox rollback. The alternative
strand test confirms a failed book does not abort other usable paths.

The retained C++/Go comparison executes the integer arithmetic and sorted
aggregation. Flow, offer, and transaction rollback expectations are checked
against the pinned C++ source and exercised by Go tests; this fixture is not
a full C++ daemon transaction replay.

`TestMPTBookAggregateOverflowRollsBackRealPayment` creates both issuances,
holdings, balances, and offers using real transactions, then submits the
overflowing payment through the engine. It covers partial and full payments
with ordinary sequences and tickets, checking TER, applied status, claimed
fee, sequence/ticket consumption, unchanged offers and owner counts, and
unchanged MPT holdings and outstanding supply.
